title: A Portrait for the Ledger
premise: True-crime podcaster Zephyrine Okonkwo has built a career proving the police wrong, so when a wealthy stranger pays him to prove that a murder at the Ashcombe estate hasn't happened yet — predicted for the fortieth anniversary dinner — he assumes a hoax. But the anonymous client's details match an unsolved death from 1985 with uncanny precision, and Zephyrine realizes someone alive today intends to complete a pattern begun four decades ago. As he infiltrates the anniversary gathering under cover of recording a commemorative episode, he discovers the client is the original killer's child, seeking absolution by preventing a copycat crime. In the end, Zephyrine must choose between exposing the truth that would destroy an innocent family's last illusion of belonging and letting a murderer walk away unnamed.
about_author: Sable Quintana spent a decade as a court stenographer before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the cadence of testimony. She lives in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Maine coast, where she writes mysteries about people who can't stop digging into other people's pasts.

chapters.title: The Advance Payment
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Okonkwo receives a cashier's check and a typed letter offering triple his fee to prove a murder will NOT occur at the Ashcombe anniversary dinner in six weeks. His producer Priya warns him it's a publicity stunt or worse. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: wary curiosity — the case smells wrong in a way he can't resist.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine digs into the 1985 death of Eleanor Ashcombe, ruled an accident on the estate grounds, and finds the letter's 'predictions' mirror its unsolved anomalies exactly. He interviews the retired detective who closed the file and catches him lying about one detail. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the thrill of a pattern emerging from cold static.

chapters.title: An Invitation Extended
chapters.summary: Posing as a podcast host covering the anniversary, Zephyrine secures an invitation from matriarch Vivian Ashcombe, who seems oddly eager for attention. He meets the scattered heirs: bitter son Marcus, fragile granddaughter Tessa, and charming family lawyer Daniel Reyes. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the uncanny warmth of a family performing itself for strangers.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Exploring the estate, Zephyrine finds Eleanor's preserved study and a hidden ledger of household accounts with pages torn out around the date of her death. A figure watches him from the garden; when he gives chase, they vanish. POV: alternating between Zephyrine and brief italicized fragments of an unknown observer. Emotional beat: the house itself feels complicit.

chapters.title: The Client Speaks
chapters.summary: A burner call finally comes: the client admits to being raised on the estate as a servant's child and claims their parent confessed to Eleanor's murder on their deathbed — and that someone inside the family now knows and plans to finish what was started. POV: Zephyrine, listening. Emotional beat: dread curdling into responsibility; the money suddenly feels like blood.

chapters.title: Tessa's Version
chapters.summary: Granddaughter Tessa, drunk and grieving her own recent loss, tells Zephyrine she found letters suggesting Eleanor had a secret child among the staff — possibly the client, possibly someone still living at Ashcombe. Marcus interrupts them with barely concealed menace. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: tenderness toward Tessa, and the first sense that belonging here could cost him everything.

chapters.title: Pages Torn Out
chapters.summary: Priya traces the cashier's check to a shell company tied to Daniel Reyes, the lawyer — but when confronted, Daniel reveals he was hired anonymously too, instructed to keep the anniversary guest list exactly as it stands. Someone is choreographing the event. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: paranoia; every ally might be a puppeteer.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal
chapters.summary: At the pre-dinner toast rehearsal, Zephyrine notices the seating chart recreates the 1985 dinner photograph down to the empty chair left for Eleanor. He realizes the killer isn't predicting the murder — they're restaging it, and the missing chair is meant for a victim not yet named. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the trap is already set and he's sitting inside it.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: During the toast, Zephyrine springs his counter-trap, swapping place cards to force the killer's hand. Marcus lunges at Tessa with the same antique letter opener from 1985 — revealed as Eleanor's secret son, avenging a mother's confession he misread. Zephyrine disarms him as guests flee; the observer from the garden turns out to be the client, Eleanor's other hidden child, who orchestrated everything to flush out the truth. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into terrible triumph.

chapters.title: What Belongs in the Ledger
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Zephyrine faces his choice: air the episode and shatter Tessa's world, or bury the ledger pages naming Eleanor's children forever. He records two versions — and releases only the solved mystery, keeping the family's secret sealed, while mailing the torn pages to Tessa to decide herself. The client vanishes, debt paid. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; some truths belong to the people who live inside them.
